title: Anant National University Artist-in-Residence Ravice Rashid Receives Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar
summary: Ravice Rashid, Artist-in-Residence at Anant National University, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi’s Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar in Folk Theatre for his work on Kashmir’s Bhand Pather.
body_html:
Ahmedabad, 10 November 2026: Ravice Rashid, Artist-in-Residence at Anant National University, has been honoured with the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar in the Folk Theatre category for Jammu and Kashmir. The award is conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, and recognises emerging artists for their contributions to India’s diverse performing arts traditions.

Ravice received the award from Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister for Culture and Tourism, at a ceremony in New Delhi. The ceremony was attended by artists, educators, researchers and officials from the Ministry of Culture.

A theatre artist and cultural activist from Wathora, Jammu and Kashmir, Ravice has spent years working to preserve and modernise Bhand Pather, Kashmir’s centuries-old folk theatre tradition. Through more than 100 street plays, he has used the traditional form to engage audiences on contemporary social issues, including environmental awareness, the Right to Information movement and sexual abuse. His performances also draw attention to the ecological challenges facing Kashmir, particularly the degradation of its wetlands and water bodies.

His work has earned him several earlier recognitions, including the Ministry of Culture Award and the Jammu and Kashmir Saqafati Markaz’s Young Personality Award.

According to the University, Ravice’s association with Anant National University reflects its emphasis on bringing Indigenous Knowledge Systems and traditional artistic practices into contemporary learning. As artist-in-residence, he has contributed to the University’s engagement with Jammu and Kashmir through cultural exchange, climate action and heritage conservation initiatives. His involvement in artist and student exchanges also gives Anant students opportunities to engage with India’s diverse artistic traditions and to understand their wider social, cultural and environmental contexts.

The University also engages artists from Jammu and Kashmir through workshops, campus events and student interactions, enabling students to learn from living cultural traditions and explore their relevance to present-day social and environmental challenges.

Anant National University said the recognition underscores the continuing relevance of India’s traditional performing arts and their ability to engage meaningfully with contemporary social concerns, and congratulated Ravice on the achievement and his sustained efforts to preserve Kashmir’s cultural heritage for newer generations.
